_meta.indication: DaTscan is a radiopharmaceutical indicated for striatal dopamine transporter visualization using SPECT brain imaging to assist in the evaluation of adult patients with suspected Parkinsonian syndromes (PS); it may be used to help differentiate essential tremor from tremor due to PS.
_meta.receipt_date: Original NDA dated March 6, 2009, received March 9, 2009

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 304 (labeled Study 1), a multicenter, single-arm study in patients with early signs/symptoms of Parkinsonian syndromes
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the documents reviewed
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, single-arm imaging study; DaTscan image outcomes were compared to a reference clinical diagnostic standard of PS or non-PS established by a consensus panel of movement disorder specialists after 36 months of follow-up; images read by blinded readers.
pivotal_trials.population: 99 adult patients with tremor and early signs/symptoms of Parkinsonian syndromes (44% female, 42% aged 65 or over, all Caucasian).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Agreement (positive and negative percent agreement) of DaTscan image results with the reference clinical diagnostic standard of PS vs non-PS.
pivotal_trials.result: Positive percent agreement across readers 77-79% (Reader A 77 [66, 87]); negative percent agreement 96% (96 [82, 100]).

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 003 (labeled Study 2), a multicenter, single-arm supportive study in patients with established diagnoses of PS or ET
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the documents reviewed
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, single-arm imaging study comparing DaTscan images (read by blinded readers including site investigators) to the investigator clinical diagnosis as the reference standard.
pivotal_trials.population: 185 adult patients with tremor and established diagnoses of PS or ET (35% female, 48% aged 65 or over, 99% Caucasian); baseline diagnoses PD 70%, ET 15%, MSA 10%, PSP 5%.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Positive and negative percent agreement of DaTscan image results with the reference clinical diagnostic standard.
pivotal_trials.result: Positive percent agreement across readers 92-97% (Reader A 93 [88, 97]); negative percent agreement 74-96% (Reader A 96 [81, 100]; Reader B 74 [54, 89]).

key_safety: No serious adverse reactions in clinical trials; most common adverse reactions (headache, nausea, vertigo, dry mouth, dizziness) each occurred in <1% of subjects. Hypersensitivity and injection site reactions have been reported post-marketing.
target_moa: Ioflupane I 123 binds reversibly to the dopamine transporter (DaT) on dopaminergic neurons concentrated in the striatum; radioactive decay of iodine 123 emits gamma radiation allowing SPECT visualization of the striata, reflecting DaT density.

advisory_committee.vote: Advisory committee held August 11, 2009 voted 11 to 2 to support a favorable risk-to-benefit determination for the drug.

description.text: Added new indication for striatal dopamine transporter visualization via SPECT brain imaging in adult patients with suspected dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication, DATSCAN is indicated as an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations for striatal dopamine transporter visualization using single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) brain imaging in adult patients with:- suspected dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB).

basis.text: The application was assigned a priority review (as supported by neurologic consultation).

citations.quote: The application was assigned a priority review (as supported by neurologic consultation);

summary.text: DaTscan received a priority review and was reviewed over three cycles; after two Complete Response letters addressing labeling (including Schedule II controlled-substance text), it was approved January 2011 with a favorable 11-to-2 advisory committee vote and one post-marketing commitment.

citations.quote: The application was assigned a priority review (as supported by neurologic consultation);
the committee voted 11 to 2 to support a favorable risk to benefit determination for the drug;
We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling text.

requirement.text: Commitment #1725: conduct a clinical trial assessing agreement between DaTscan imaging results and diagnostic outcomes among non-Caucasian and Caucasian patients, designed to allow comparison between the two groups.

citations.quote: 1725. To conduct a clinical trial that assesses the agreement between DaTscan imaging results and diagnostic outcomes among non-Caucasian and Caucasian patients. This trial will be designed and conducted in a manner that allows a comparison of the results between the non-Caucasian and Caucasian patients.

date.text: Complete Response letters issued September 8, 2009 and December 22, 2009

citations.quote: The original submission was on March 6, 2009 and a Complete Response letter was issued on September 8, 2009 (deficiencies related to need for package insert labeling update). The second review cycle began with the applicant's resubmission on October 26, 2009 and concluded with issuance of a Complete Response letter on December 22, 2009 in which the single deficiency related to the need to incorporate Controlled Substance text in the package insert.

basis.text: First CRL related to the need for a package insert labeling update; second CRL related solely to the need to incorporate Controlled Substance (Schedule II) text in the labeling.

citations.quote: • A Complete Response letter was issued based solely upon the need to have controlled substance text incorporated in the labeling.
